headline: Discussed moving the Nailed It sculpture from 143 Pine Street; Simard Payne Memorial Park considered as new site.
summary: Updates came in on projects funded in the FY26 budget, including the Zebra mural maintenance, now finished, and the Farmers' Market mural, expected by the first week in October. The group also discussed moving the Nailed It sculpture, a maintenance plan for older public art, and updating the public art map. Members approved the August 10, 2026 minutes and set the next two meeting dates.
decisions: Approved the meeting schedule for October 19, 2026 and November 16, 2026, 5-0.

decision_titles: Meeting dates for October 19 and November 16, 2026
plain_text:
1 
 
 
 
LEWISTON PUBLIC ART COMMITTEE  
Monday, September 14, 2026, at 6:00 pm 
Lewiston City Hall, First Floor Administrative Conference Room 
Meeting Minutes – DRAFT 
Committee members in attendance: Deanna Ehrhardt, Chairperson; Darby Ray; James Lysen; Courtney 
Schlachter; and Gerald Walsh; and Scott Harriman, Council Liaison. 
Committee members absent: Scott Harriman, Council Liaison (excused) 
Others present: Kathryn Ruth, Community Development Manager 
1) Call Meeting to Order: 
Chairperson Ehrhardt called the meeting to order at 6:00 pm. 
 
2) Approve Meeting Minutes for August 10, 2026 
Ms. Ray moved and Mr. Lysen seconded the motion to approve the committee meeting minutes 
of August 10, 2026.  The vote was (5-0).  Motion passed. 
 
3) Update on projects funded through the FY26 (July 1, 2025 – June 30, 2026) Budget  
which remain to be finished during the next few months: 
a. Window Wrap projects to be designed by local artists  $  7,500   
b. Lewiston Farmers’ Market Association (LFMA) Mural   $12,000 
c. Community initiatives      $  2,202 
Zebra Project Maintenance is the final project 
        d. Nameplates for 5 sculptures for all costs (design, site visit, $11,697 
  drawings, materials and installation) plus $200 for drilling  
        e.   Street Art and Mitigation of Graffiti in the Downton:  $  9,302 
  1.  Downtown Street Art Project:  $4,302 
  2.  Marcotte Park – Jude’s Place:  $5,000 
 
Members shared their updates on the projects which were completed or in progress.  These 
are very positive and low-cost projects for the community.  All projects had contracts and  
payments were processed for the last fiscal year. 
Below are brief notes on the projects: 
 
a.  For the Window Wrap projects to be designed by local artists organized and administered by  
L/A Arts, also includes the Bus Station and the Hannaford Bus Stop.  Mr. Walsh reported that the  
window wraps have gone to print with the design approved.  There is a Memorandum  
of Understanding with the LA Transit Committee.  The draft was changed.  The project is on  
track for the first location to be completed by the end of the month.  This is the Hannaford Bus  
Stop.  The second approval is for the actual Bus Station.  It has the same design with stickers  
featuring a variety of crows.  The artists working on them will find it easier to put the stickers on
2 
 
              when it is not a whole window.  Both entry ways will have framing around the doors.  How much  
the artist can do without blocking the view will be determined.  Mr. Walsh mentioned that the  
artist is Claudio Jimenez, a former Bates College graduate, who now works at Gather to Grow. 
 
b.  The Lewiston Farmers’ Market Mural is moving along well after receiving more public input 
than previously expected.  This resulted in design changes which always take time to address.  
The project is behind schedule by 1 to 2 weeks and will not be finished by the end of September.   
It is expected to be finished by the first week in October.  The project involves spray paint and is  
expected to take 10 days.   The owner was very cooperative.  The building was power washed  
and it was scrapped.  It has received a thick heavy layer of primer.    
 
c.  The Zebra Mural Maintenance Project required a lift so originally, it was anticipated that it  
could be coordinated with another L/A project, however, this did not come to fruition. The  
budget for materials was very tight.  Mr. Walsh borrowed a truck and went to get the lift and  
then operated it over the weekend for a full day to save funds.  It was really a 2-person job;  
however, he managed to do quite well and learned a bit about using a lift.  There were more 
areas damaged on the mural than originally thought so the artist had to scrap some of 2-3 colors  
off and then enhanced those areas.  Overall, the Zebra maintenance project went quite well.   
Serafim Yssolo, the artist who painted the building at Lionel Potvin Park, completed the project.   
While this maintenance is not restoration and will not save the art piece indefinitely, it will add  
several years to its life.  Many positive comments have been received.  
 
d.  Nameplates for the 5 sculptures project moved forward with the $200 bill for drilling issued. 
Both Deputy PW Director Bates and Ms. Ruth worked on this project to move it forward.  This is  
the culmination of a project that began several years ago.  Ms. Ruth will have photos taken for  
the record as well as assist Public Works in verifying that the plaques are all installed with the 
correct art pieces. 
 
e.  The Street Art and Mitigation of Graffiti in the Downtown consists of two projects and both 
were awarded to Wicked Illustrations. 
(1)  Downtown Street Art Project – has been advertised with a request for recommendations for 
locations to mitigate graffiti with butterflies and flowers.  Residents and interested parties were  
invited to Wicked Illustrations to paint the art.  The art would only be installed after the receipt 
of a completed building owner’s permission slip. For Wings of Change, the participating artists 
were Savannah Sinclair, Taylor Newbeck, Leo Goddard, Jennifer Roberts Powers, Jamie 
Campbell, Bryce Cloutier, Lynn Walkiewicz, Lily Croteau and Melanie Therrien.  Wings were 
painted during a community paint day and wings were painted by students.   
The locations and artists were: 
1- 43 Lisbon St. - Jamie Campbell - Scarab and flowers  
2- 43 Lisbon St. Canal side - Bryce Cloutier - Butterfly  
3- Orbit Hairstyling - Melanie Therrien - flowers and monarchs  
4-  Franco Center - Lily Croteau - blue butterfly  
5- Peck Building - Savannah Sinclair - 250 anniversary butterfly, Jennifer Powers - dragonfly and 
flowers, Lynn W - ladybug, student butterfly wings, community butterfly wings  
6- 207 Barber Shop - Leo Goddard - Luna moth  
7- Canal Plaza Alley - Taylor Newbeck - butterfly and flowers  
 
A different artist was highlighted each day on social media with a photo of their wings and a 
short bio and/or statement and then again after installation. Some wings have yet to be installed
3 
 
 
              (2) Marcotte Park, Jude’s Place - The Artists were Melanie Therrien, Jamie Campbell and Bryce  
Cloutier.  Images of Locations to cover up graffiti had been located.  The artists have painted  
butterflies,  bees and a flower hopscotch to install at the next available date when the weather  
is clear. Some areas, such as the beaver and arch, were planned to be repaired directly with  
paint and then clear coated. The beaver in the park was repainted and given a glow up, then  
clear coated. The graffiti on the fish arch was covered up with matching paint, the art touched  
up and everything was clear coated. Graffiti was covered up with butterflies on the stairs, a  
flower hopscotch, butterfly and other flowers covered up graffiti in the walking path. A bee is in  
the middle of the tables covered up vandalism there and then a caterpillar covered up more  
vandalism around the tables. The final touch was an addition to the caterpillar including a stick,  
leaves and pupa installed as well as a few more flowers. Some of the art in the walkway had  
been torn up so the artists repaired that damage.  A nonslip additive was added to the clear coat  
of any art that was in the walkway. 
  
       4)   Budget for FY27 (July 1, 2026 – June 30, 2027)   
              For the 4 art projects approved from the Call for Artists, a new agreement was drafted for the 
Uneeda Biscuit & J. Dulac & Sons Public Art Mural utilizing the new Small Project  
              construction type agreement she was instructed to use.  As it does not cover art projects, 
              Ms. Ruth extracted important sections from the PAC typical agreement.  This was  
              completed while the organizer for the project, Joseph Phillipon, obtained addendums 
for the project.  Although the L/A Arts coordinated project for the Artist Michael Rich titled 
The Lew Mural at the Skateboard Park is not taking place until late Spring 2027, she would like 
to get this project under contract also. Then there are two other projects to address.  Ms. Ruth  
noted that she continues to handle more work than usual from other positions as there are  
some vacancies and movement in the Department that has continued. 
  
       5)    Discuss the removal of Public Art – Nailed It – from 143 Pine Street as Public Works has been 
               notified that the property has been sold.  While the property has been sold, Public Works is still  
mowing it.  The Chairperson followed up on this with the owner to determine details and  
if the artwork can stay on site for a while as a new location is located.  She will continue to  
contact the owner understanding her busy schedule.  Several locations were originally 
discussed such as Simard Payne Memorial Park, Kennedy Park and other areas.  Ms. Ruth had  
brought a list of city owned vacant lots to the meeting that was passed around for review in  
August and the parks seem to be the best properties to start to review to see if a location  
will work.  It was agreed that a permanent location is needed as well as a plan for funding  
and/or locating contractor/s who would volunteer their services to help.  Mr. Walsh  
described his efforts and his discussion with a representative of the Maine Mill.  Ms. Ruth noted 
that we need to determine who will need to approve the move for this piece of art.  Committee 
members thought a location in Simard Payne Memorial Park would provide the Nailed It  
sculpture the respect and appreciation that this piece of art should have.  It is important to have 
a quotation from Public Works to move Nailed It to the park.  Ms. Ruth will contact Public  
Works and look into who would approve moving this sculpture. 
    
       6)    Discuss the need for a Maintenance Plan for the City’s Public Art to include when to upkeep and 
when to decommission.  Ms. Schlachter had reviewed the information she had located back at 
the August committee meeting from her research.  She will gather more information and report 
to the Committee once she has had time to contact other communities, talk to the artists and/or 
review other cities’ approaches.  This is a project that will take time to develop properly and will 
need to be tailored to Lewiston’s needs.
4 
 
Projects that have been mentioned that need a maintenance plan and work are the  
following:   (a) some of the older sculptures such as Women’s Suffrage which has been  
subject to wear; (b) Walking Trees which needs power washing; and (c) the Flags which are  
starting to come apart.  There was a discussion about the Walking Tree Structure as it appears  
there is spotting and flaking.  It is definitely time to perform maintenance on this piece of art. 
 
Much of the discussion centered on how the Committee needs to determine its obligations in  
terms of artwork that may have a shelf Life and cannot be restored.  A number of pieces need 
attention and may be able to be addressed with repainting, however, some may need to be 
retired.  This will require research to determine the best approach. 
     
       7)    Discussion on the last published list of Public Art financed through the City as well as private  
               art.  L/A Arts has this list and had an intern update the electrical boxes with photos from 
re-visiting the sites.  While most boxes got a paint update, a few had changed so new photos 
were taken.  The new Alley murals need to be added.  L/A Arts needs to determine how to label 
the art as the map is very crowded in locations.  L/A Arts is trying to locate a copy of the original 
spreadsheet with the City’s pieces of art on it.  A former employee’s Gmail account was 
scrubbed so there is no access anymore for the research that took place on a lot the Public Art.  
This would need to be reconstructed or locate someone who has access.  It was thought that the 
individual who put the spreadsheet together is still in the area so there will be an attempt to 
make contact first.  There is a good chance that the former employee kept a copy of the files 
and has the information the Committee needs.  The Art map that L/A Arts had created and has 
available on its site is limited in adding more projects.  It does not have a goggle map and there 
is no ability to use it in the field to connect with goggle.  There was a lengthy discussion about 
updating the map and the plan which could be used to promote Public Art in the City.  This is a 
work in progress and will need some time due to the amount of public art. 
 
As she has time, Ms. Ruth agreed to review the meeting minutes available in the City’s records 
to identify art projects that have taken place and the approximate time of discussion. 
 
      8)    Other business, if any, to come before the Committee: 
 There was no further business.  
 
      9)    Next Meeting:  
The Committee agreed to the following meeting schedule given the holidays taking place on the 
date of their next meeting as well as having a holiday during the week the November committee 
meeting would normally be scheduled to be held at 6:00 pm in the First Floor Administrative  
Conference Room. 
 
Mr. Lysen moved and Ms. Ray seconded the motion to approve the committee meeting  
schedule as follows:  Monday, October 19, 2026 and Monday, November 16, 2026. 
The vote was (5-0).  Motion passed. 
 
     10)    Motion to adjourn: 
Ms. Lysen moved and Mr. Walsh seconded the motion to adjourn the meeting.  The vote was   
(5-0).  Motion passed. 
The Meeting was adjourned at 6:51 pm. 
 
 
Minutes submitted by: 
Kathryn Ruth, Secretary Pro-Tem
